subject: tech
title: Robots and Sensors
about: Robots as machines that follow a program written by people, sensors as their way of noticing (camera eyes, microphone ears, touch and light sensors), robot vacuums, factory arms, delivery robots and toy robots programmed with arrows, steps in order, bugs, why robots are good at repeating a job, how they do not feel or decide like people, smart speakers and their wake word, and how life changed before and after these machines. NC K2-CS-02 (hardware parts and what they do), K2-AP-01 (daily processes as algorithms) and K2-IC-01 (life before and after new technology). Read it together: the tablet reads every question and choice aloud.
tip: Be the robot: let him give you three steps in order (stand up, turn, clap) and follow them exactly, even if the order is funny.

cards.note: A robot is a machine that follows a program, a list of steps written by people.

cards.q: A robot follows a program. Who writes the program?
cards.note: Robots do what they are told. People think of the steps and type them in.

cards.q: What does a robot use to notice the world around it?
cards.note: A sensor is a part that senses something, like light, sound or a bump, and tells the program.

cards.q: A robot's camera works like which part of your body?
cards.note: A camera lets the robot see shapes and colors, just like eyes.

cards.q: A robot's microphone works like which part of your body?
cards.note: A microphone hears sounds. A smart speaker uses one to hear your voice.

cards.q: A robot vacuum bumps into a wall and turns. Which sensor felt the wall?
cards.note: A bumper or touch sensor feels a bump, like your hand feeling a wall in the dark.

cards.q: The room gets dark and a robot stops. Which sensor noticed the dark?
cards.note: A light sensor measures how bright it is. Night lights that turn on by themselves use one too.

cards.q: Before robot vacuums, how did people clean the floor?
cards.note: New machines change how people live. A robot vacuum cleans while people do other things.

cards.q: In a factory, a robot arm puts the same part on every car. Why is a robot good at this job?
cards.note: Robots are great at doing the same job again and again, exactly the same way.

cards.q: A small robot rolls down the sidewalk with a pizza inside. What is it?
cards.note: Delivery robots use cameras and sensors to find the way and to stop for people.

cards.q: A toy robot moves when you press arrow buttons: forward, forward, turn. What did you make?
cards.note: A list of steps the robot follows is a program. You are the programmer!

cards.q: You tell a robot: get a bowl, pour cereal, pour milk. What is this list of steps called?
cards.note: An algorithm is a list of steps in order. People follow them too, like a recipe.

cards.q: A robot pours the milk before the bowl is there. What was wrong?
cards.note: Robots follow steps exactly in order. Put the bowl first, then pour.

cards.q: A robot turns left when it should turn right. What does its program have?
cards.note: A bug is a mistake in a program. Finding and fixing it is called debugging.

cards.q: Can a robot feel happy or sad like you do?
cards.note: A robot may show a smiley face, but it does not feel. It only follows its program.

cards.q: In a video, a robot seems to choose a toy. Who really chose it?
cards.note: A robot does not decide like a person. It follows the choices people wrote into the program.

cards.q: A smart speaker sits quietly until you say its special word. What is that word called?
cards.note: The speaker's microphone listens for its wake word, then it listens to your question.

cards.q: Before robot arms, who put the parts on cars in a factory?
cards.note: People did the heavy, repeated work by hand. Now robots help, and people fix and program the robots.
